'''Gustavo Alfonso Ayón Aguirre''' (born April 1, 1985)<ref name="Puertorico2009.fiba.com">{{cite web |url=http://puertorico2009.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/facm/player/p/eid/4042/pid/65095/sid/4042/tid/328/profile.html |title=FIBA.com: 2009 FIBA Americas Championship for Men Player profile |publisher=Puertorico2009.fiba.com |access-date=2013-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129050121/http://puertorico2009.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/facm/player/p/eid/4042/pid/65095/sid/4042/tid/328/profile.html |archive-date=2016-01-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref> is a Mexican politician<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/estados/2026/03/31/tiro-de-3-basquetbolista-gustavo-ayon-renuncia-a-morena-se-une-a-mc-y-maynez-lo-candidatea-en-nayarit/|title=Tiro de 3: Basquetbolista Gustavo Ayón renuncia a Morena, se une a MC y Máynez lo candidatea en Nayarit|newspaper=[[El Financiero]]|date=March 31, 2026|access-date=April 1, 2026|language=es}}</ref> and former professional [[basketball]] player. He represented the senior [[Mexico men's national basketball team|Mexican national basketball team]] in international [[national team]] competitions. Standing at a height of {{height|ft=6|in=10}}, he played at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. Ayon is a two−time [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection.

==Early life and college career==
Gustavo was born April 1, 1985, to parents Ayón Ayón and mother Linda Ayón.

Ayón attended at the [[Universidad Popular Autónoma del Estado de Puebla]], in Mexico, for three years of college.  He was named the [[Most Valuable Player]] of the Mexican College Championship Tournament, in leading his team to the National Championship.<ref name=cc>{{cite news|title=Men's basketball adds 6-foot-11 Mexican all-star |url=http://www.sjsuspartans.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5600&ATCLID=509008 |access-date=25 October 2014 |work=sjsuspartans.com |date=20 July 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928021600/http://www.sjsuspartans.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5600&ATCLID=509008 |archive-date=September 28, 2011 }}</ref>

Following that season, he signed with [[NCAA]] [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State University]].<ref name=cc/> However, Ayón never played for the Spartans, instead choosing to sign with a Mexican professional team, [[Halcones de Xalapa|Halcones UV Xalapa]].<ref name="basketpedya.com"/>

==Professional career==
[[File:Gustavo_Ayon_and_Nene_Washington_at_Orlando_010.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Gustavo Ayon (19) of the [[Orlando Magic]] and [[Nenê]] of the [[Washington Wizards]].]]

===Mexico===
In the 2006 season, Ayón saw some action off the bench for [[Halcones UV Xalapa]], as the team finished second in the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketpedya.com/Acc003InfTeam.php?ideq=4734&temporada=2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112193044/http://www.basketpedya.com/Acc003InfTeam.php?ideq=4734&temporada=2006|archive-date=2013-11-12|url-status=usurped|title=Kiến Thức Bóng Rổ, Cá Độ Bóng Rổ Thabet -}}</ref>  Ayón cracked the team's starting lineup the following season, and eventually led Halcones to back-to-back Mexican league titles, in 2007–08 and 2008–09.<ref name="basketpedya.com">{{Cite web|url=https://basketpedya.com/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112193042/http://www.basketpedya.com/Acc002InfJug.php?idjug=62727|url-status=usurped|title=Kiến Thức Bóng Rổ, Cá Độ Bóng Rổ Thabet -|date=May 18, 2023|archivedate=November 12, 2013}}</ref>  He averaged 10.2 points and 8.1 rebounds per game in 2007–08, and improved on that by averaging 13.2 points and 7.8 rebounds per game the following season.<ref name="basketpedya.com"/>  In what turned out to be his final game for the team, Ayón turned in a dominant, 24-point, 20-rebound, performance in leading his club to a 94–90 overtime victory over [[Soles de Mexicali]], that clinched their second consecutive league title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italia/nazionali/992/halcones_uv_xalapa_ayon_celebrate_mexican_title_after_edging_soles_in_ot.html |title=Halcones UV Xalapa, Ayon celebrate Mexican title after edging Soles in OT |publisher=Sportando.net |access-date=2013-11-12}}</ref>

===Spain===
Following the 2008–09 season, Ayón signed with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] of the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.baloncestofuenlabrada.com/?se=noticia&n=386 |title=Baloncesto Fuenlabrada S.A.D |publisher=Baloncestofuenlabrada.com |access-date=2013-11-12}}</ref>  In November 2011, Ayón was named the Spanish League's [[ACB Player of the Month Award|ACB Player of the Month]].

===NBA===
In December 2011, Ayón signed with the [[New Orleans Hornets]], of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], after paying [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] with a $1.5-million buy-out clause. Ayón received a three-year contract, with the last year being a team option.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/news/story?id=1436456&s=bas&type=story |title=Fuentes: El mexicano Gustavo Ayón firma con New Orleans - ESPN: Deportes |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-01-01 |access-date=2013-11-12}}</ref>

On July 11, 2012, Ayón was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]], in a [[sign-and-trade deal]] for [[Ryan Anderson (basketball, born 1988)|Ryan Anderson]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic Acquire Gustavo Ayon From Hornets|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-gustavo-ayon-hornets_071112|work=NBA.com|access-date=24 February 2013}}</ref>

On February 21, 2013, Ayón was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], along with guards [[Ish Smith]] and [[JJ Redick]], for guards [[Beno Udrih]] and [[Doron Lamb]], and forward [[Tobias Harris]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks Acquire J.J. Redick, Gustavo Ayon and Ish Smith from Magic|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-jj-redick-gustavo-ayon-and-ish-smith-magic|work=NBA.com|access-date=24 February 2013}}</ref>

On July 25, 2013, he was waived by the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-request-waivers-gustavo-ayon | title=Bucks Request Waivers on Gustavo Ayon | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=July 25, 2013 | access-date=July 25, 2013}}</ref>

On July 29, 2013, Ayón was claimed off waivers by the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-awarded-gustavo-ayon-waivers |title=HAWKS AWARDED GUSTAVO AYON OFF WAIVERS |work=NBA.com |date=July 29, 2013 |access-date=July 29, 2013}}</ref> On February 12, 2014, Ayón scored a career high 18 points, in a 83–104 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140212/ATLTOR/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Raptors 104, Hawks 83 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811172604/http://www.nba.com/games/20140212/ATLTOR/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2014-08-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 28, 2014, it was announced that Ayón would miss the rest of the 2013–14 season, following successful surgery to repair a right shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/gustavo-ayon-injury-update-0 |title=GUSTAVO AYON INJURY UPDATE |work=NBA.com |date=February 28, 2014 |access-date=February 28, 2014}}</ref>

===Return to Spain===
On September 23, 2014, Ayón signed a two-year deal with Spanish club [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] coached by [[Pablo Laso]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid officially signs Gustavo Ayon to a two-year deal|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/135514/real-madrid-officially-signs-gustavo-ayon-to-a-two-year-deal.html|date=September 23, 2014|access-date=September 23, 2014|work=Sportando.com}}</ref> In the 2014–15 season, Real Madrid won the [[2014–15 Euroleague|EuroLeague]], after defeating [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], by a score of 78–59 in the [[2015 EuroLeague Final Four|league's finals]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is Euroleague champion for record ninth time!|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=251&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=18 July 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> Real Madrid eventually finished the season by also winning the [[2014–15 ACB season|Spanish League championship]], after a 3–0 series sweep in the [[2015 ACB Finals|Spanish League finals series]] against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]]. With that championship, Real Madrid thus won the [[European Basketball Triple Crown|triple crown]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid make it 4 out of 4|url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/06/24/en/football/real_madrid/1435176357.html|access-date=24 June 2015|work=marca.com|date=24 June 2015|language=es}}</ref>

Ayón was named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round]], in the first week of the playoffs, in the 2014–15 season,<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/|title=Latest News | EuroLeague|date=May 18, 2023|website=Euroleague Basketball}}</ref> and in week nine of the regular season of the 2015–16 season.<ref name="auto"/>

On January 4, 2016, Ayón was named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month]], for December 2015.<ref name="auto"/> On May 6, 2016, he was named to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]], for the [[2015–16 Euroleague|2015–16 EuroLeague]] season.<ref name="auto"/> In May 2016, he was named the [[ACB Player of the Month|Player of the Month in the Spanish Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/acb/250230/gustavo-ayon-is-mvp-of-the-month-in-spain/|title=Gustavo Ayon is MVP of the month in Spain|date=May 24, 2016|website=Eurohoops}}</ref>

On July 14, 2016, Ayón signed a new three-year contract with Real Madrid.<ref name="auto"/>

In May 2018, Real Madrid won the [[2017–18 EuroLeague]] championship, after defeating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Doğuş]] in the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four|final game]] with 85–80.<ref name="EuroLeague18Champ">{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is 2018 EuroLeague champion|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=260&seasoncode=E2017#!report|access-date=20 May 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=20 May 2018}}</ref> Over 17 EuroLeague games, Ayón averaged 9.6 points, 6.1 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game.

In June 2018, Ayón helped guide Real Madrid to the 2017-18 ACB Spanish League Championship by defeating [[Saski Baskonia|Kirolbet Baskonia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2781942-luka-doncic-real-madrid-beat-kirolbet-baskonia-in-2018-acb-championship|title = Luka Doncic, Real Madrid Beat Kirolbet Baskonia in 2018 ACB Championship|website = [[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref>

In June 2019, Ayón helped lead Real Madrid to the 2018-19 ACB Spanish League Championship by defeating [[FC Barcelona Lassa]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9qxr9jc9a4m53gud/domestic-league-playoffs-efes-real-wins-league-titles|title = Domestic league playoffs: Efes, Real wins league titles!| date=18 May 2023 }}</ref>

===Russia===
On July 26, 2019, Ayón signed a one-year deal with [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/item/9tqt9f8xrph75rmf|title=Zenit shocks market, signs Ayon!|work=Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL|access-date=26 July 2019}}</ref> He averaged 12 points, 5 rebounds and 2 assists per game. Ayón parted ways with the team on July 26, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zenit, Gustavo Ayon part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/zenit-gustavo-ayon-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 26, 2020 |date=July 26, 2020}}</ref>

===Return to Mexico===
On September 30, 2020, Ayón signed with [[Astros de Jalisco]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Gustavo Ayon inks with Astros de Jalisco |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gustavo-ayon-inks-with-astros-de-jalisco/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 30, 2020 |date=September 30, 2020}}</ref>

===Puerto Rico===
On September 19, 2021, Ayón signed with [[Capitanes de Arecibo]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Skerletic|first1=Dario|title=Capitanes de Arecibo ink Gustavo Ayon|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/capitanes-de-arecibo-ink-gustavo-ayon/|newspaper=Sportando|date=September 19, 2021|access-date=September 19, 2021}}</ref>

Ayón led the [[Capitanes de Arecibo]] to the Championship of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN) of Puerto Rico.  This latest championship is the 16th professional championship for Ayón.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/basquetbol/nota/_/id/9537220/gustavo-ayon-capitanes-de-arecibo-campeones-bsnpr|title=Equipo de Anuel AA y Gustavo Ayón, campeón en Puerto Rico|date=18 November 2021}}</ref>

On August 20, 2022, Ayón announced his initial retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketballinsiders.com/news/gustavo-ayon-retires-from-professional-basketball/ | title=Gustavo Ayon retires from professional basketball | date=22 August 2022 }}</ref> However, in April 2023 he announced that he would come out of retirement to play for [[Venados de Mazatlán]],<ref name="basketnews.com">{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-188739-gustavo-ayon-comes-out-of-retirement.html|title=Gustavo Ayon comes out of retirement|website=basketnews.com}}</ref> where he played a single game on April 26, 2023 against [[Halcones de Ciudad Obregón]] scoring 7 points and grabbing 7 rebounds.

==National team career==
Ayón has been a member of the senior [[Mexico men's national basketball team|Mexican national basketball team]] since 2007. He played [[center (basketball)|center]] for the seventh placed Mexicans at the [[2007 FIBA Americas Championship]], and the fifth placed team at the [[2008 Centrobasket]].<ref name="Puertorico2009.fiba.com"/>

In 2013, Ayón led Mexico to victory in the gold medal game against [[Puerto Rican national basketball team|Puerto Rico]] at the [[2013 FIBA Americas Championship|FIBA Americas Championship]].  Ayón was named to the [[FIBA AmeriCup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]], and was named [[FIBA AmeriCup Most Valuable Player|the MVP of the tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/9/11/4720312/fiba-americas-championship-2013-results-mexico-puerto-rico |title=FIBA Americas 2013 championship results: Mexico takes FIBA Americas title with thrilling win over Puerto Rico |date=11 September 2013 |publisher=SBNation.com |access-date=2013-11-12}}</ref>

In August 2014, Ayón led Mexico to victory in the gold medal game against Puerto Rico at the [[2014 Centrobasket]].  Ayón was named the MVP of the tournament.<ref>[http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/mexico-wins-home-centrobasket-2014/ Mexico wins home Centrobasket 2014]</ref> Later that month, he joined Mexico for the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 FIBA World Cup]].

In 2015, Ayón was named to the [[2015 FIBA Americas Championship]] All-Tournament Team, after tallying 17.7 points per game (2nd in the tournament), 12.4 rebounds per game (1st in the tournament), 3.5 assists per game (7th in the tournament), 1.3 steals per game (3rd in the tournament), and 1.2 blocks per game (1st in the tournament).

In June 2018, Ayón helped lead Mexico to a 78–70 victory over Team USA in [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/29/mexico-shocks-usa-basketball-world-cup-qualifying|title=Mexico shocks USA Basketball in World Cup qualifying round|website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>
